An image is not always the most robust route to inference.

I study reliable sensing under limited sampling and measurement noise, connecting optical measurement design, image reconstruction and direct inference from single-pixel measurements. I now work on time-domain diffuse optical tomography for brain imaging, inferring 3D distributions of optical properties from photon time-of-flight measurements. My long-term aim is to help robots interpret the physical world from raw measurements and physical models.

Outside the lab: basketball, fitness and travel.

Image-free sensing can be more robust to measurement noise than reconstructing an image first.

The Lift Spectrum: How Measurement-to-Space Adaptivity Shapes Robustness in Image-Free Single-Pixel Sensing

arXiv preprint · 2026

Single-pixel segmentation · clean training, noisy testing

Explore the study
Contribution & evidence
  • Robustness: direct inference overtakes the strongest tested reconstruction-first baselines as measurement noise increases, when all models are trained on clean data.
  • Representation: a content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift turns the measurement sequence into spatial task features.
  • Training: task-prioritized loss scheduling (TPLS) shifts emphasis from auxiliary reconstruction to the sensing task.
  • +3.1–21.7 pp foreground mIoU at 20 dB Gaussian noise, 3.13% sampling
  • Reconstruction-first still leads without measurement noise
  • Proof of concept on a real single-pixel bench, no fine-tuning

Generalized sparse Hadamard single-pixel Imaging

Optics Express · 2025

Measurement design · theory and optical experiments

Contribution & evidence
  • Tunable sparse Hadamard patterns retain orthogonality and improve noise resilience, with two training-free modes and a sparsity-dependent noise model tested in simulations and through-scattering optical experiments.
  • Orthogonal sparse patterns built from lower-order Hadamard bases
  • Two training-free operating modes
  • Sparsity-dependent noise theory tested in simulation and optical experiments

Contribution & evidence
  • Loop differential ghost imaging reduces spatial noise asymmetry for 1D optical phased-array line modulation; validated with a noise-symmetry metric, numerical simulations and spatial-light-modulator-generated line patterns.
  • Algorithm designed for optical phased-array line modulation
  • A metric that quantifies the spatial symmetry of noise
  • Validated in simulation and with SLM-generated line patterns

Current directions

  1. Acquisition-aware single-pixel sensing

    Single-pixel sensing that accounts for the conditions under which measurements are acquired, tested in optical-bench experiments; manuscript in preparation.

  2. Question answering from measurements

    Exploratory

    Testing whether a frozen vision–language model can answer questions about a scene directly from its single-pixel measurements.

  3. 3D optical brain imaging

    Time-domain diffuse optical tomography: inferring the 3D distribution of optical properties from photon time-of-flight measurements.

Research code

  • STSF-TPLS

    Image-free segmentation from single-pixel measurements with a content-adaptive lift and task-prioritized loss scheduling; code and pretrained weights (PyTorch).

  • Comparison-of-SPI-DLs

    Eight deep networks and correlation ghost imaging, benchmarked on one shared Hadamard acquisition (PyTorch).

  • SHSI

    Sparse Hadamard pattern generation, simulation and reconstruction examples (MATLAB).

  • LDGI

    Loop differential ghost imaging designed for 1D optical phased-array line illumination (MATLAB).

  • TGIs-Entry

    Reference implementations of traditional, differential and normalized ghost imaging (MATLAB).

  • remote-gpu-trainer

    Open-source agent skill for Claude Code and Codex that runs, verifies and delivers GPU experiments.
